### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/net/ethernet/stmicro/stmmac/dwmac4_descs.c`**
   - The function `dwmac4_rx_check_timestamp` was modified to handle endianness correctly.
   - Three variables (`rdes0`, `rdes1`, and `rdes3`) were introduced, which store the values of `p->des0`, `p->des1`, and `p->des3` after converting them from little-endian to CPU endianness using the `le32_to_cpu` function.
   - The original checks for ownership and context descriptor were updated to use the new variables (`rdes0`, `rdes1`, and `rdes3`) instead of the original descriptor fields (`p->des0`, `p->des1`, and `p->des3`).

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications in the `dwmac4_descs.c` file are directly related to fixing the endianness issue in the `dwmac4_get_timestamp` function. By ensuring that the descriptor values are correctly interpreted according to the CPU's endianness, the patch addresses a bug that was previously introduced in the PTP support for GMAC4. This change enhances the reliability of timestamp retrieval in the driver, ensuring that it works correctly across different CPU architectures.

You will be given the root cause of a bug, the commit message and the corresponding patch.
        You need to extract all code statements that lead to the bug from the patch, based on the root cause and the commit message.

        Root cause:
        The bug was caused by the `dwmac4_get_timestamp` function not properly handling endianness when accessing descriptor fields. Since the GMAC IP is little-endian and can be used on both big and little-endian CPUs, failing to convert the descriptor values from little-endian to the CPU's native endianness led to incorrect timestamp retrieval and potential data corruption.
        
        Commit message:
        net: stmmac: handle endianness in dwmac4_get_timestamp

GMAC IP is little-endian and used on several kind of CPU (big or little
endian). Main callbacks functions of the stmmac drivers take care about
it. It was not the case for dwmac4_get_timestamp function.

Fixes: ba1ffd74df74 ("stmmac: fix PTP support for GMAC4")
Signed-off-by: Alexandre Torgue <alexandre.torgue@st.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>  
        
        Patch:
        diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/stmicro/stmmac/dwmac4_descs.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/stmicro/stmmac/dwmac4_descs.c
index 20299f6f65fc..736e29635b77 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ethernet/stmicro/stmmac/dwmac4_descs.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ethernet/stmicro/stmmac/dwmac4_descs.c
@@ -241,15 +241,18 @@ static inline void dwmac4_get_timestamp(void *desc, u32 ats, u64 *ts)
 static int dwmac4_rx_check_timestamp(void *desc)
 {
 	struct dma_desc *p = (struct dma_desc *)desc;
+	unsigned int rdes0 = le32_to_cpu(p->des0);
+	unsigned int rdes1 = le32_to_cpu(p->des1);
+	unsigned int rdes3 = le32_to_cpu(p->des3);
 	u32 own, ctxt;
 	int ret = 1;
 
-	own = p->des3 & RDES3_OWN;
-	ctxt = ((p->des3 & RDES3_CONTEXT_DESCRIPTOR)
+	own = rdes3 & RDES3_OWN;
+	ctxt = ((rdes3 & RDES3_CONTEXT_DESCRIPTOR)
 		>> RDES3_CONTEXT_DESCRIPTOR_SHIFT);
 
 	if (likely(!own && ctxt)) {
-		if ((p->des0 == 0xffffffff) && (p->des1 == 0xffffffff))
+		if ((rdes0 == 0xffffffff) && (rdes1 == 0xffffffff))
 			/* Corrupted value */
 			ret = -EINVAL;
 		else
--

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
own = p->des3 & RDES3_OWN;
ctxt = ((p->des3 & RDES3_CONTEXT_DESCRIPTOR)
```
Reason:
The `dwmac4_get_timestamp` function accesses the descriptor fields directly from the `dma_desc` structure without converting them from little-endian to the CPU's native endianness. This oversight can lead to incorrect values being read on big-endian CPUs, resulting in erroneous timestamp retrieval and potential data corruption.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
unsigned int rdes0 = le32_to_cpu(p->des0);
unsigned int rdes1 = le32_to_cpu(p->des1);
unsigned int rdes3 = le32_to_cpu(p->des3);
own = rdes3 & RDES3_OWN;
ctxt = ((rdes3 & RDES3_CONTEXT_DESCRIPTOR)
```
Reason:
The patch introduces the use of the `le32_to_cpu` function to convert the descriptor fields from little-endian format to the CPU's native endianness before accessing them. This ensures that the values are correctly interpreted regardless of the underlying architecture, thus fixing the bug related to timestamp retrieval.
